subject: Night shift: streaming chat p99 tailwave during peak — urgent customer escalation
messages:
From: Anika Patel <anika@fastretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: support@fastretail.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 23:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Night shift: streaming chat experiencing p99 spikes

Karthik —

We started seeing a sharp p99 regression on the streaming chat endpoint during our 22:00–00:00 PT peak window tonight. Key numbers: p95 hovered ~420ms (normal ~300ms) but p99 jumped to ~1.6s (baseline ~450ms). Error rate for the SSE connections rose to ~1.8% (disconnects + 502s). Throughput (tokens/sec) stayed within expected range, but connection churn increased by ~27% during the burst.

Attached: server traces from a handful of affected clients, and a short screen grab of the admin console showing connection drops. This is affecting our support chat and increasing SLAs breached. Can your team triage? We need a mitigation plan (even something temporary) until root cause is found.

--
Anika Patel
Head of Platform Reliability, FastRetail
anika@fastretail.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Support <support@fastretail.com>

Anika — thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments. We see the alert as well (ALERT-7863). I'm escalating this to the on-call engineering lead and our ops team.

Short plan while we triage:
- I'll notify Eng (cc'd) to look for cache/throttling anomalies and any recent kernel changes that could affect SSE paths.
- If the impact remains high, we can enable a temporary circuit-breaker to force degraded (non-streaming) fallback for a minority of traffic to prevent widespread SLA breaches.
- We'll update you with ETA for a mitigation in the next 30–60 minutes.

Cc: Marissa — can you coordinate customer comms and finance escalation if needed?

Karthik

Forwarding FastRetail thread — flagged as a high-impact customer escalation (VIP, multiple SLA breaches possible). Please treat as priority. Quick context: spike is concentrated in SSE/WebSocket streaming paths during their peak evening window; earlier tonight we pushed a kernel selection tweak for small-sequence attention optimizations in the hosted runtime (can cause micro-behavior changes under high connection churn).

Immediate asks for Eng (Grace / Jonas):
- Confirm whether the recent kernel change is active for the streaming fleet serving FastRetail (which model variants, which shards).
- Check KV/prefix cache hit-rate, and whether cache eviction/promotion patterns look abnormal ("cache melt" hypothesis).
- Look at connection churn metrics and LB backpressure signs.

Customer comms: Karthik — I recommend we offer the temporary fallback and a credit if we can't provide firm ETA within 2 hours. I'll prepare a short message for the customer if you want to send it after Eng triage.

Attachments: customer logs from Anika.

Marissa
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2026 00:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Night shift: streaming chat experiencing p99 spikes

Marissa / team — triage summary so far (quick, actionable):
- Confirmed: the small-sequence attention kernel change was rolled to the streaming pool serving FastRetail earlier this week and is active on ~35% of shards.
- Observed: sudden surge in prefix-cache misses correlated with connection churn. Miss storms are increasing KV lookups and causing tail amplification on p99 for sessions that experience frequent reconnects.
- Also saw a subtle increase in async-queue durations on the SSE workers (likely due to continuous batching interacting poorly with a high churn of very short-lived sessions).

Immediate mitigations we can enact (low risk):
1) Hot rollback of the kernel tweak on the streaming pool serving FastRetail (start with canary rollback to 10% then 100% if successful) — ETA ~45–90 minutes to verify.
2) Enable per-customer circuit-breaker to route 20% of traffic to the non-streaming (polling) endpoint as a temporary fallback — config change, ETA ~20 minutes.
3) Increase prefix-cache size for affected shard set to reduce eviction storms — needs a coordinated restart, ETA ~2–3 hours and higher risk.

Proposed immediate action: do (2) now and start (1) as a canary. I'll kick off rollback if canary looks good. Assigning jobs: Jonas to run the rollback; I'll enable the circuit-breaker and monitor.

Grace
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2026 01:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Night shift: streaming chat experiencing p99 spikes

Update / timeline:
- Circuit-breaker configured and rolled to 20% of FastRetail sessions at 01:18Z. Early telemetry: those sessions show p99 back within baseline (p99 ~480ms). No customer-visible errors for fallback cohorts.
- Started canary rollback of the kernel tweak at 01:30Z on 10% of streaming shards. Canary nodes show normalized prefix-cache hit-rate and reduction in async-queue duration.
- If the canary stays green over the next 30 minutes, I'll promote rollback to 100% (full rollback across FastRetail-serving shards).

Customer comms in progress — Karthik/Marissa feel free to share this short note with Anika: we have an active mitigation (fallback + canary rollback) and expect to fully roll back the change within ~1.5 hours if canary remains healthy. We'll follow up with a technical post-mortem and proposed guardrails to prevent recurrence.

Jonas
Tech Lead, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Night shift: streaming chat experiencing p99 spikes — mitigation live

Anika — quick update from our side:
- We've enabled a temporary fallback for ~20% of your streaming sessions; those sessions are seeing p99 return to baseline.
- We've started a canary rollback of a recent runtime kernel change that correlates with the regression; early canaries are positive and show restored cache hit rates. Full rollback is targeted within 1.5 hours.
- Next steps: we'll complete rollback, monitor for re-occurrence through your peak, and deliver a post-mortem by EOD PST tomorrow with a list of concrete guardrails (canary thresholds, auto-fallback rules, and an opt-in safety mode for high-churn customers).

We apologize for the disruption — we're treating this as a high-priority exec-level incident. I or Marissa will update you as the rollback completes.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
